findings.title: Negative remainder cents are assigned to the latest parts
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 3: “Distribute any remainder cents one per part, earliest parts first. This must hold for negative totals as well as positive ones.”
findings.trigger: A negative total has a cent count that is not evenly divisible by ways.
findings.consequence: The extra negative cents appear in the last parts instead of the earliest parts.
findings.evidence: Executing split_evenly(Decimal('-0.01'), 3) returned [Decimal('0'), Decimal('0'), Decimal('-0.01')]; the criterion requires [Decimal('-0.01'), Decimal('0'), Decimal('0')]. Likewise, -10.00 split three ways returned [-3.33, -3.33, -3.34] instead of [-3.34, -3.33, -3.33].

findings.title: Totals containing fractional cents are rounded before splitting
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 2: “Guarantee the parts sum exactly to total, with no lost or invented cents.”
findings.trigger: total is a Decimal amount that is not an exact whole number of cents.
findings.consequence: The returned parts sum to a rounded value rather than the supplied total.
findings.evidence: Executing split_evenly(Decimal('1.001'), 3) returned [Decimal('0.34'), Decimal('0.33'), Decimal('0.33')], whose sum is Decimal('1.00'), not Decimal('1.001'). Executing it with Decimal('0.005') and 2 returned [Decimal('0.01'), Decimal('0')], summing to Decimal('0.01').

reasoning: Execution confirmed the required list length, Decimal element type, exact sums for whole-cent positive and negative totals, positive remainder ordering, and ValueError behavior for ways of 0 and -1. The explicit negative-order and unrestricted exact-total guarantees nevertheless fail under the concrete conditions reported above.
